# package cp

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-iec60870-5/cp"
```

Package cp encodes and decodes the binary time tags of IEC 60870-5-4 (subclause 6.8): CP16Time2a (elapsed milliseconds), CP24Time2a (minute, second, millisecond), CP32Time2a (adds the hour) and CP56Time2a (a full date and time).

They are shared by the companion standards that use them: IEC 60870-5-101 and -104 use CP16, CP24 and CP56; IEC 60870-5-103 uses CP32 for event time tags and CP56 for clock synchronization. The ASDU codecs of those standards build on this package; applications normally use their re-exported types (for example asdu.Timestamp).

## Functions

### func AppendCP16

```go
func AppendCP16(b []byte, d time.Duration) []byte
```

AppendCP16 appends d as CP16Time2a: elapsed milliseconds 0..59999. A duration outside that range is clamped.

### func AppendCP24

```go
func AppendCP24(b []byte, t Timestamp, loc *time.Location) []byte
```

AppendCP24 appends t as CP24Time2a in loc (nil means UTC).

### func AppendCP32

```go
func AppendCP32(b []byte, t Timestamp, loc *time.Location) []byte
```

AppendCP32 appends t as CP32Time2a in loc (nil means UTC): CP24Time2a followed by the hour octet with the SU flag.

### func AppendCP56

```go
func AppendCP56(b []byte, t Timestamp, loc *time.Location) []byte
```

AppendCP56 appends t as CP56Time2a in loc (nil means UTC). A time outside 1970..2069 cannot round-trip through the two-digit year and goes out flagged invalid.

### func ParseCP16

```go
func ParseCP16(b []byte) (d time.Duration, ok bool, err error)
```

ParseCP16 decodes a CP16Time2a. Values above 59999 are returned as they are; ok is false for them.

## Types

### type Timestamp

```go
type Timestamp struct {
	time.Time

	// Invalid is the IV flag: the time is not reliable.
	Invalid bool
	// Substituted is the GEN flag (bit 7 of the minute octet's RES1
	// position in IEC 60870-5-4, used as "substituted time" by
	// IEC 60870-5-101/-104 implementations): the time was not taken at the
	// source of the information but added by intermediate equipment.
	Substituted bool
	// SummerTime is the SU flag (CP32Time2a and CP56Time2a): the time is
	// daylight saving time.
	SummerTime bool
	// NoWeekday reports a CP56Time2a whose day-of-week field is 0. The
	// field ranges 1..7 (IEC 60870-5-4, CP56Time2a); stations that do not
	// use it send 0. When it is set the encoder writes 0 again instead of
	// the day of the week of Time, so a time tag that is passed on or
	// mirrored keeps the octets it came with.
	NoWeekday bool
}
```

Timestamp is a time tag. Which fields are meaningful depends on the format it travels in:

  - CP24Time2a decodes onto 0001-01-01 00:mm:ss.mmm: only the minute, second and nanosecond of Time are meaningful, and the receiver has to supply the hour and date. On encode only those fields are used.
  - CP32Time2a adds the hour (and SU) and decodes onto 0001-01-01 hh:mm:ss.mmm; the receiver supplies the date.
  - CP56Time2a carries a full date and time. Its year is two digits: 70..99 decode as 1970..1999 and 0..69 as 2000..2069.

The wire formats carry no time zone; times are converted to and from the location given to the codec functions.

A zero Time encoded as CP56Time2a is written as 2000-01-01 with the invalid flag set. A received CP56Time2a with a field out of range, or a date that does not exist, decodes to the zero Time with Invalid set.

#### func Now

```go
func Now() Timestamp
```

Now returns a valid time tag for the current time.

#### func ParseCP24

```go
func ParseCP24(b []byte, loc *time.Location) (Timestamp, error)
```

ParseCP24 decodes a CP24Time2a in loc (nil means UTC). Out-of-range fields are normalized by time.Date and flagged invalid.

#### func ParseCP32

```go
func ParseCP32(b []byte, loc *time.Location) (Timestamp, error)
```

ParseCP32 decodes a CP32Time2a in loc (nil means UTC). An hour above 23 is flagged invalid.

#### func ParseCP56

```go
func ParseCP56(b []byte, loc *time.Location) (Timestamp, error)
```

ParseCP56 decodes a CP56Time2a in loc (nil means UTC).
